identity.notes: The app keys every probe by its advertised name (the code the cloud registers), and uses the platform's peripheral handle only as a connection locator it re-learns from each scan. Whether the probe's address is public or rotating is not established, so prefer the name.

manufacturer_data.description: Company ID 0x074C, payload = the ProbeAdvertisementRecord (14 bytes or more).

methods.notes: Scan actively with duplicates allowed and no service-UUID filter, which is what the app does (low-latency scan mode). Keep a result only if the local name is exactly 8 characters long AND the manufacturer data under 0x074C is present. A pHin monitor's "pHin-xxxx" name is 9 characters and fails the test, so the two families never collide in the app's scanner. Which advertising PDU carries the name and which the manufacturer data (advertisement or scan response) is not established.

host_compatibility.basis: The vendor app scans, connects and writes to the probe through the platform stack on Android.
The same app ships for iOS and carries iOS-specific branches in its probe code (scan duration, live-mode byte masking, ORP sign handling).

manufacturer_data.description: The app accepts an advertisement as an EcO record only if its manufacturer data is keyed 074c (the BLE library formats the little-endian company ID as four lowercase hex digits and strips it from the value, on Android and on iOS alike). 0x074C is not listed in the Bluetooth SIG company-identifier registry as fetched 2026-09-28 (0x074B and 0x074D belong to unrelated companies), so it is either an unlisted assignment or a squatted value. Treat it as "an advertisement shaped like the one documented here", and require the 8-character name as well.

identification.notes: The second condition the app applies, a local name of exactly 8 characters, has no identification key (a length test is neither a prefix nor an exact name); it is stated in discovery.methods[0].notes. The name's format beyond its length is not established: it is the probe's code as registered with the vendor cloud and has not been seen on air. Whether the probe advertises service f3a00001-f0a2-9b06-0c59-1bc4763b5c00 is not established either; the app does not filter on it.

device.name: iopool EcO / EcO Salt pool water monitor
device.notes:
A sealed floating probe from iopool (Belgium), sold in the EcO Start pack, that measures pH, ORP (the app calls it disinfection potential), water temperature and conductivity and reports its battery level. The FCC filing (2AVNQECO-V1, model "EcO v01") shows a Bluetooth 4.0 LE radio with an integral antenna and nothing else: no Wi-Fi, no Sigfox. The optional iopool Connect box (gateway generations IGW and I10 to I40 in the app) relays probe readings to Wi-Fi; it is a separate product and out of scope, as are the Ecotab chlorine-tablet dispenser and the iopool cloud.
EVIDENCE BASE. Everything below is `reported`: read out of the vendor's Android app (React Native, Hermes bytecode, v2.43.6). No capture is held, nothing has been replayed, and no open implementation of the BLE side exists (the one community integration, mguyard/hass-iopool, polls the vendor cloud). The scalings of pH and temperature are `hypothesis`.
THE READ PATH NEEDS NO CONNECTION. The probe broadcasts its latest measurement in manufacturer-specific advertisement data under company ID 0x074c (on air: ff 4c 07 then the record). The app scans continuously with duplicates allowed and no service filter, and takes an advertisement as an EcO record when it has a local name exactly 8 characters long AND manufacturer data under 0x074c. The name is the probe's code, which the vendor cloud registers against the owner's pool. See payload_formats.ProbeAdvertisementRecord for the byte layout: format version, mode, sequence, pH (int16 BE), ORP (int16 BE), temperature (uint16 BE), conductivity (uint16 BE), a packed activity/battery byte, and an 11-bit time of day in minutes after 00:00 UTC. A record repeats in advertisements until the next measurement, so deduplicate on (name, sequence, minutes).
THE CONNECTED SURFACE is small and needs no pairing. Service f3a00001-f0a2-9b06-0c59-1bc4763b5c00 carries: a command characteristic (f3a00002) that takes one-byte opcodes (0x04 monitoring mode, 0x05 maintenance/standby mode, 0x01 a reset whose effect is not established); a clock characteristic (f3a00008) that takes the Unix time in seconds as 8 bytes little-endian; a beep characteristic (f3a00009) that takes the uint16 LE value 200; a live-mode characteristic (f3a0000a) that takes [count, 0x00]; and a software-version characteristic (f3a00011) read as ASCII. The app writes everything with response, and on EVERY connection it writes the clock first, right after service discovery.
LIFECYCLE. A new or wintered probe advertises records with mode 3 (maintenance). The app finds a new probe by waiting for such a record, after the owner turns the probe upside down and back, then connects, sets the clock, reads the software version, writes 0x04 and disconnects. Wintering is the reverse: connect, write 0x05, disconnect. Mode numbers in the record (1 standard, 2 live, 3 maintenance, 4 backup) are NOT the command opcodes.
THE CLOCK MATTERS. The record carries only the time of day, taken from the probe's own clock, and the app rebuilds the date: today at that minute (UTC), or yesterday if that would be more than 15 minutes in the future. If the result is more than 30 minutes old or more than 5 minutes ahead, the app treats the probe clock as drifted, stamps the reading with the current minute, and reconnects to reset the clock. It also reconnects once a day for the first measurement. A client that never connects will see the probe's clock wander.
SHARED UUID BASE. The -f0a2-9b06-0c59-1bc4763b5c00 base is also used by Blueriiot's Blue Connect analyser (f330xxxx; see blueriiot-blue-connect.yaml), so never identify on the base alone.
NOT THIS DEVICE. Earlier notes attributed the f4000001 "transport" and f4100001 "OTA" services and SIG service 0xfe63 to the EcO. In the app they belong to the Connect gateway, the Ecotab dispenser and adopted pHin monitors respectively (see protocol_details.uuids_that_are_not_this_device). The app has no firmware-update path for the EcO at all. The iopool app also reads pHin monitor advertisements; that format belongs to the separate phin-pool candidate (research-notes/phin-pool-monitor.md) and is not described here.

openness.notes: iopool publishes a read-only cloud API (pools and their latest measurement) but nothing about the probe's radio protocol. Everything below was recovered from the vendor app.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: No pairing window exists. The turn-over gesture in setup wakes a probe into maintenance mode; it is not a pairing step.

exclusivity.notes: Nothing bonds, so there is nothing to forget. Whether the probe accepts a second central while one is connected is not established. A Connect gateway is itself a BLE client of the probe.
exclusivity.recovery: Close the vendor app, and unplug an iopool Connect gateway if there is one near the pool, then retry.

pairing.notes: The app's probe path connects, discovers services and writes, with no bonding call anywhere in it (reported). The measurement path needs no connection at all.

safety_advisory.detail: The probe broadcasts raw sensor values. The vendor keeps the per-probe pH and ORP calibration in its cloud (the app sends raw live samples from a calibration wizard there), so a local client sees the uncalibrated value. The pH and temperature scalings in this spec are inferences, not facts read from the app. Check a reading against a test strip before adding acid, chlorine or salt, and follow the chemical supplier's handling instructions. This spec is independent of iopool.
safety_advisory.summary: Readings decoded from this spec are uncalibrated raw values with partly inferred scalings; pool chemicals dosed on a wrong pH or ORP reading can irritate skin and eyes.

credentials.notes: The probe has no Wi-Fi and no BLE authentication. Anything in radio range can read its measurements and switch its mode. The pack's QR code is a cloud credential and is not used on the BLE link.

factory_reset.description: The procedure below is the only reset-like operation in the app. It is listed as a candidate so an owner knows it exists, not because it is known to return the probe to factory state. After it, expect to have to re-activate the probe (monitoring-mode opcode) if the app's behaviour is any guide.
factory_reset.effect: No owner-facing factory reset is documented, and the probe holds no bond or credential, so a BLE client has nothing on the device to clear. The pool link lives in the vendor cloud. The app's pool settings offer a "reset EcO" action that sends opcode 0x01; what it clears on the probe (stored measurements, clock, mode) is not established.

procedures.basis: Vendor app (com.iopool 2.43.6): the pool-settings reset action connects, writes 0x01 to the command characteristic and disconnects.
procedures.name: BLE reset opcode 0x01

steps.action: Connect to the probe, write the current time to f3a00008 as on every connection.
Write 0x01 with response to f3a00002-f0a2-9b06-0c59-1bc4763b5c00 (command reset), then disconnect.
Watch the next advertisements for the mode byte, to learn which state the probe is in afterwards.

methods.description: The vendor app's own activation exchange, minus the cloud calls. Wake the probe, find its maintenance-mode advertisement, connect, set its clock, optionally read its software version, write the monitoring-mode opcode, and disconnect. From then on the probe broadcasts measurements (mode 1 records) that any listener can decode.
methods.name: Wake by turning over, then switch to monitoring mode over BLE (no account)

steps.action: Take the probe in your hand, turn it upside down and then back upright.
steps.notes: The app's activation screen asks for this gesture. The FCC internal photos show a two-lead switch beside the buzzer that is consistent with a tilt switch, but that is not confirmed.

steps.expect: Advertisements with an 8-character name and manufacturer data 0x074C whose byte 1 (mode) is 3.

steps.action: Scan for an 8-character name with manufacturer data 0x074C and record byte 1 equal to 3. Keep the name: it is the probe's code.
steps.notes: The app gives up after 5 s by default and reports the probe as not found.

steps.action: Connect without pairing and discover services.
Write the current Unix time to f3a00008-f0a2-9b06-0c59-1bc4763b5c00 (command set_time).
steps.notes: The app does this on every connection, before anything else.

steps.action: Optionally read f3a00011-f0a2-9b06-0c59-1bc4763b5c00 and decode it as ASCII: the software version.
Write 0x04 with response to f3a00002-f0a2-9b06-0c59-1bc4763b5c00 (command enter_monitoring_mode), then disconnect.

steps.expect: Records with byte 1 = 1 and a new sequence number. How long the first one takes is not established; the app tells the owner the probe needs an acclimatisation period in the water before its first reliable analysis.

timing.notes: Both are the vendor app's defaults, not device limits. The app scans in low-latency mode with duplicates allowed.

causes: The probe was not woken: repeat the turn-over gesture.
The probe is already in monitoring mode: look for mode 1 records under the same name instead.
The scanner filters duplicates or by service UUID. The app does neither.
Out of range. The app tells owners to move closer to the pool.
Another central holds the probe: the vendor app, or an iopool Connect gateway relaying readings (whether the probe takes a second central is not established).
The probe's clock was never set or has drifted. Connect and write set_time; the app does so at least daily.
troubleshooting.symptom: Measurements carry the wrong time of day.

cloud.local_alternative: The BLE activation in the primary method uses no account, token or cloud value, and the measurements are broadcast in the clear.
cloud.provider: iopool (account on AWS Cognito; app API over GraphQL)

methods.description: What the vendor app does. The owner creates an account and a pool, scans the QR code of the EcO Start pack, and then the app runs the same BLE exchange as the primary method and registers the probe's code and software version against the pool in the vendor cloud. Measurements then reach the cloud through the owner's phone, or through an iopool Connect gateway. The cloud side is not documented here.
methods.name: Vendor app with an iopool account

steps.action: Create an iopool account and a pool in the vendor app, and scan the pack's QR code.
Follow the app's EcO activation screen: turn the probe over when asked.
Run the BLE activation exchange and link the probe code to the pool.

setup.notes: Nothing is provisioned: no credentials, no bond, no network. But a new or wintered probe sits in maintenance mode and the app does not treat its records as measurements until it has been switched to monitoring mode over BLE, so setup is required in that sense. The whole BLE exchange is recovered from the vendor app and needs no account or token. Confidence medium: it is the vendor's own implementation, read rather than replayed, and whether a factory-fresh probe advertises before the wake gesture has not been observed.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds the probe to a phone. Any listener in range decodes its advertisements, and any central can connect and write its commands. Moving a probe to another pool or account is a cloud operation: the app asks whether to link an already-activated probe to the new pool.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project, and no capture of real traffic is held. Every byte layout below comes from static analysis of the vendor app (com.iopool 2.43.6), so every fact is `reported` at best, and the scalings marked `hypothesis` are inference on top of that.

device.type: Floating pool and spa water monitor (pH, ORP, water temperature, conductivity) that broadcasts its readings in BLE advertisements

variants.notes: The standard probe (FCC model "EcO v01"). The app warns that it is not salt-water compatible.

The salt-water probe. The app's probe-type values are ECO, ECO_SALT and PHIN, and its EcO handling applies to any type containing "ECO", so both probes run the same parser and commands. The type comes from the vendor cloud's record of the probe, not from the advertisement, and no on-air difference is known. The salt level itself is entered from a test strip, not measured by the probe.

entities.name: pH
entities.notes: From the advertisement (payload_formats.ProbeAdvertisementRecord.ph), no connection needed. Uncalibrated, and the 1/100 scale is a hypothesis. Skip mode 2 and mode 3 records.

entities.name: ORP
entities.notes: From the advertisement (ProbeAdvertisementRecord.orp). Uncalibrated. Decode as signed.

entities.name: Water Temperature
entities.notes: From the advertisement (ProbeAdvertisementRecord.temperature). The 0.01 C scale is a hypothesis; check it against a thermometer.

entities.name: Conductivity (raw)
entities.notes: From the advertisement (ProbeAdvertisementRecord.conductivity). Raw integer, unit not established.

entities.name: Beep
entities.notes: Connect, write set_time, write the beep, disconnect. The probe floats in the pool, so this is how to find it.

entities.name: Start Live Mode
entities.notes: Five back-to-back measurements by default, broadcast as mode-2 records.

entities.name: Activate (Monitoring Mode)
entities.notes: Activates a new probe or wakes one from wintering.

entities.name: Winter Standby (Maintenance Mode)
entities.notes: The app's wintering. Measurements stop being ingested until the probe is activated again.

evidence.app_static_analysis: The vendor's Android app, com.iopool 2.43.6 (React Native with a Hermes bytecode bundle), decompiled to pseudo-code and read. It established: the scan (continuous, duplicates allowed, no service filter, low-latency); the discovery test (an 8-character local name plus manufacturer data keyed 074c); the advertisement record's layout, signedness and masks, and the battery and minutes formulas; the mode numbering and which modes the app ingests; how it rebuilds the measurement date and when it declares clock drift; the connect sequence (12 s timeout, service discovery, clock write on every connection); the GATT map of service f3a00001 and the operation on each characteristic; the opcodes 0x01, 0x04 and 0x05; the 8-byte little-endian Unix-seconds clock payload; the beep payload (uint16 LE 200) and the three-beep test; the live-mode payload [count, 0] with its default of 5 and the calibration wizard's 21; the activation, wintering and reset flows; and which nearby UUIDs belong to the Connect gateway, the Ecotab and pHin. Not established from the app: the pH, ORP and temperature scalings (the app forwards raw integers to the cloud) and anything the probe does that the app does not exercise. Nothing was copied.

artifacts.artifact: com.iopool 2.43.6 (iopool, React Native with Hermes bytecode; Android APK)

Radio (BLE 4.0 only), battery, antenna, SoC and the welcome guide.
How the app's manufacturer-data key maps to bytes on the air.
Cloud-only and read-only: no BLE, no device control.

evidence.documentation_review: FCC ID 2AVNQECO-V1 (iopool SA, Belgium, granted 2020-04-15): the grant page, the test report (model EcO v01, Bluetooth 4.0 LE, 3.7 V internal battery, integral antenna), the internal photos (TI CC2640R2F) and the welcome-guide exhibit (two-year battery, keep in water, start guide). The Bluetooth SIG company-identifier registry (fetched 2026-09-28) has no entry for 0x074C.
evidence.negative_findings: No firmware-update path for the EcO exists in the app: its firmware-URL configuration belongs to the Connect gateway and the Ecotab, and no TI over-the-air-download service UUID appears anywhere in the bundle. No notification subscription and no bonding call exists in the probe path. The f400 and f410 services and 0xfe63 are not the EcO's. No capture of the probe exists in any source this project holds, and no public BLE-level write-up of it was found.
evidence.open_questions: See remaining_unknowns. The cheapest first checks with a probe in hand: one passive scan (the name format, whether f3a00001 is advertised, the format-version byte, the record length, and the temperature and pH raw values next to a thermometer and a test strip), then one connect and read of f3a00011.
evidence.open_source_review: innoveit/react-native-ble-manager, the app's BLE library: DefaultPeripheral.java (Android) and ios/Helper.swift key manufacturer data by the company ID formatted as four lowercase hex digits and strip the ID from the value, which is what turns the app's 074c key into company ID 0x074C and fixes where offset 0 of the record sits. mguyard/hass-iopool: the Home Assistant integration polls the vendor's read-only REST API for each pool's latest measurement (already converted to pH, mV and degrees) and exposes no device control, so there is no cloud control surface to fall back on either.

initialization.description: Right after service discovery, write the current Unix time (command set_time: 8 bytes, seconds, little-endian). The bytes change every second, so this step is documentation: a client builds them itself.
initialization.notes: The vendor app does this on every connection before any other command, including connections made only to resynchronise the clock.

ProbeAdvertisementRecord.description: The manufacturer-specific advertisement data after the two company-ID bytes (on air: ff 4c 07, then these bytes). Offsets count from the first byte after the company ID. Multi-byte fields are BIG-endian, unlike most BLE payloads. The app reads bytes 0 to 13, so a record is at least 14 bytes; whether longer records carry more is not established. Layout from the vendor app's parser (reported); scalings marked hypothesis are inference.

fields.description: Record format version. Values seen in the field are not known; the app does not branch on it.
fields.name: format_version

fields.description: The probe's mode when it took this measurement. The app ignores maintenance records for measurement purposes, keeps live records for calibration only, and for backup records prefers a timestamp that this record does not carry. What "backup" means on the probe is not established.
fields.name: mode

fields.description: Measurement counter. In live mode it counts the run from 1. Wraparound behaviour is not established.
fields.name: sequence

fields.description: pH. The app sign-extends the 16-bit value (reported) and forwards the raw integer to the cloud. The 1/100 scale is inference: it fits the range and the app's calibration stability test (a spread under 5 raw units). Uncalibrated.
fields.name: ph

fields.description: Oxidation-reduction potential. Raw = millivolts is inference from the pool range (the app's advice targets 650 to 800 mV). The app sign-extends it on iOS only; its Android build reads the same bytes unsigned, so a negative ORP shows there as 65536 minus the magnitude. Decode as signed. Uncalibrated.
fields.name: orp

fields.description: Water temperature. Unsigned big-endian (reported). The app forwards the raw integer and never scales it itself, so the scale is inference: 0.01 C, the encoding the Blue Connect uses on the same UUID base. 0.1 C is the main alternative. Check against a thermometer before trusting it.
fields.name: temperature

fields.description: Conductivity, raw. Unit and scale are not established. The app parses it but does not upload it with the measurement.
fields.name: conductivity

fields.description: Top two bits of byte 11. Meaning not established. The app uploads 1 in place of 0.
fields.name: activity

fields.description: Low six bits of byte 11, times 2 (reported: the app's own formula). The field can express up to 126; clamp to 100.
fields.name: battery

fields.description: 11 bits: all of byte 12 as the high bits and the top three bits of byte 13 as the low bits, i.e. byte12 * 8 + (byte13 >> 5). Minutes after 00:00 UTC on the probe's clock when the measurement was taken (see parse_rules for the date). The low five bits of byte 13 are not used by the app.
fields.name: minutes_of_day

parse_rules: Accept only advertisements whose local name is exactly 8 characters and whose manufacturer data is keyed 0x074C (on air: ff 4c 07 ...). Offsets start after the company ID.
Every multi-byte field is big-endian. pH and ORP are signed; temperature and conductivity are unsigned.
minutes = byte12 * 8 + (byte13 >> 5). measured_at = today 00:00 UTC + minutes; if that is more than 15 minutes in the future, subtract one day.
If measured_at is more than 30 minutes in the past or more than 5 minutes in the future, the probe clock has drifted: the app then uses the current minute instead and reconnects to write set_time.
The same record repeats in advertisements until the probe measures again. Treat a record as new only when (name, sequence, minutes) changes.
Treat mode 3 (maintenance) records as not measurements, and mode 2 (live) records as a calibration run, as the app does.

fields.description: The whole characteristic value as ASCII text. Length and format not established.
fields.name: software_version

parse_rules: Read the characteristic and decode every byte as ASCII.

calibration.description: The app's calibration wizard asks the owner to rinse the sensors and hold the probe in a reference solution, starts a live run of 21 measurements, and accepts the run when the spread (max minus min) of the channel being calibrated over the collected samples is under 5 raw units; otherwise it asks the owner to keep the probe in the fluid and repeats. The raw samples go to the vendor cloud, which keeps the calibration and the date of the last pH and ORP calibration. Nothing calibration-related is written to the probe (reported). A local client therefore reads uncalibrated values and has to do its own two-point calibration if it wants better.

connect_sequence.description: What the vendor app does every time it connects (reported): connect with a 12 s timeout, discover services, write set_time, then the operation (read f3a00011; or write an opcode, the beep, or the live-mode count), then disconnect. It holds no connection open and subscribes to nothing.

hardware.description: From the FCC filing for 2AVNQECO-V1 (test report and internal photos): model "EcO v01", Bluetooth 4.0 LE only across 2402-2480 MHz, an internal integral antenna, a 3.7 V internal battery, a Texas Instruments CC2640R2F SoC (marking legible in the internal photo), an 8-pin companion part whose marking is not legible (possibly serial flash), a buzzer, and a two-lead switch beside it. The welcome-guide exhibit gives a two-year battery life with no recharging, and says the probe must stay in the water once its cap is off. The vendor's current product page describes a newer generation with a replaceable battery and sensors; whether its radio protocol differs is not established.

measurement_time.description: The record carries only minutes after 00:00 UTC from the probe's own clock; there is no date and no age. The probe's clock is set by set_time. See the parse rules on payload_formats.ProbeAdvertisementRecord for how the app rebuilds the timestamp, and when it decides the clock has drifted. The app also resynchronises the clock with the first measurement it sees each day.

command_opcodes.0x04: enter monitoring mode (activate, wake from wintering)

record_modes_and_opcodes.description: Two numberings that look alike and are not. The mode byte in the advertisement record reports the probe's state; the opcode written to f3a00002 requests a state. Both from the vendor app (reported).
record_modes_and_opcodes.notes: No other opcode appears in the app. What the probe does with any other byte is not established.

record_mode_byte.1: standard: a scheduled measurement, the one to ingest
record_mode_byte.2: live: part of a run started with start_live_mode
record_mode_byte.3: maintenance: a new, wintered or standby probe

test_vectors.description: Constructed from the app's parser to pin byte order, signedness, masks and the minutes split. They are NOT captures: the format-version byte 0x01 and every value are invented, and the decoded pH and temperature use this spec's hypothesis scalings.

vectors.notes: ORP ff 38 is -200 mV signed. The vendor's Android build would read 65336 here. Byte 13's low five bits (0x1f) are ignored.
A maintenance record: what the app waits for when adding a probe, and not a measurement.

uuids_that_are_not_this_device.description: UUIDs found near the EcO's in the vendor app that belong to other products. Recorded because earlier notes attributed them to the EcO, and that is the wrong turn the next reader would take. All reported, from the app code that uses each one.

entries.belongs_to: iopool Connect BLE-to-Wi-Fi gateway (service, write, read). Used by the app's gateway setup, which also fetches the gateway's firmware URL from the vendor cloud config.
Ecotab chlorine-tablet dispenser (service, write, read). The dispenser's own firmware update and API run through it.
Adopted pHin monitors, a separate family with its own advertisement format (phin-pool candidate).
Blueriiot Blue Connect (not in the iopool app). Same UUID base as the EcO, different vendor.

remaining_unknowns: Nothing here has been seen on air. The advertised name's format (beyond its 8-character length), whether f3a00001 is advertised, and which PDU carries the manufacturer data are not established.
Whether 0x074C is an unlisted assignment or a squatted company ID.
The pH scale (1/100 is a hypothesis), the ORP unit (mV is a hypothesis) and the temperature scale (0.01 C is a hypothesis; 0.1 C is the alternative).
The conductivity field's unit and scale, and the meaning of the two activity bits.
The format-version values in use, whether records longer than 14 bytes exist, and what the low five bits of byte 13 carry.
What mode 4 (backup) means on the probe, and what the reset opcode 0x01 clears.
The beep value's unit, the live-mode measurement interval, and the standard-mode measurement and advertising intervals.
Whether a factory-fresh probe advertises before the turn-over gesture, and whether the gesture is sensed by the switch seen in the FCC photos.
Whether the probe accepts a second central while the vendor app or a Connect gateway is connected.
Whether the full property sets of the f3a0 characteristics include read or notify beyond what the app uses.
Whether the newer EcO generation with a replaceable battery and sensors speaks the same protocol.
Whether and how the probe's firmware can be updated. The app has no path for it.

enter_maintenance_mode.description: Switch the probe to maintenance (standby) mode, which the app calls wintering; it advertises mode-3 records and the app stops ingesting its measurements. The app offers it when the water is too cold for the probe. One byte, written with response.

enter_monitoring_mode.description: Switch the probe to monitoring mode: it measures on its own schedule and broadcasts mode-1 records. The app sends it to activate a new probe and to wake one from wintering. One byte, written with response.

reset.advanced_reason: Its effect is unknown. It may clear the probe's stored measurements or return it to its unactivated state, in which case it stops broadcasting measurements until it is re-activated with the monitoring-mode command. The probe is sealed, so there is no button to recover with.
reset.description: The app's "reset EcO" action from the pool settings. One byte, written with response. What it does on the probe is not established.

set_time.description: Set the probe's clock. 8 bytes: the Unix time in whole seconds (UTC, rounded), little-endian. The app builds all 8 bytes from a 64-bit value; the template writes the low 32 bits and zero-fills the high 32, which is exact until 2106. Write with response, first thing on every connection (see initialization).

unix_time.description: Seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, from the client's clock at the moment of writing.

beep.description: Sound the probe's buzzer once. The app writes the uint16 little-endian value 200 (bytes c8 00); the unit is not established (200 ms is a plausible reading). Its buzzer test connects, beeps three times 500 ms apart, and disconnects. Write with response.

start_live_mode.description: Put the probe into live mode for a run of back-to-back measurements, broadcast as mode-2 records whose sequence counts up from 1 (the app treats sequence 1 as the start of a run). Two bytes: the count, then 0x00. The app's default count is 5, and its calibration wizard asks for 21. The interval between live measurements is not established. Write with response.

count.description: Number of live measurements to take. The app's iOS branch masks it to 8 bits; its Android branch does not, which only matters above 255.

characteristics.name: Live-mode counter
characteristics.notes: The app only ever writes this characteristic. Earlier notes called it notify, but nothing in the app subscribes to it or reads it.

characteristics.name: Software version
characteristics.notes: Read once at activation. The whole value is decoded as ASCII text and stored by the vendor cloud as the probe's firmware version; see payload_formats.ProbeSoftwareVersion. Its length and format are not established, so no fixed-width format block is declared.

services.name: EcO probe service
services.notes: The probe's only vendor service in the app (reported). The UUID base is shared with Blueriiot's Blue Connect, so the service says "this design house", not "an EcO". Properties below are what the app does with each characteristic; the full property set of each is not established.
